visuals.heading: 5 Research Lanes for Humanities Graduates

items.text: Here is the full picture before the detail.
All five of those are real, current jobs in India today.

blocks.heading: Underneath the Five Very Different Job Titles

items.text: Turning a messy pile of interviews, documents, or data into one clear, defensible finding
Every one of these five lanes pays for the same underlying move: synthesis.
You do not have to pick a research lane by guessing which one sounds most impressive at a family gathering.
For academic research, write one short literature review.
A 20-minute honest conversation with a working policy analyst, market researcher, UX researcher, or M&E coordinator tells you more about the daily reality than a semester of reading about the field.
An academic historian, a policy analyst, a UX researcher, and an NGO M&E officer do genuinely different daily work, for different pay, on different timelines.
A PhD is the longest, lowest-paying, and highest-commitment lane on this list.
Only the top 6% of NET-qualified candidates in a subject receive a JRF slot in a given cycle.

blocks.heading: Academic Research: NET-JRF to Phd

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Academic research pays the least early (JRF is Rs 37,000/month) and takes the longest, but only 6% of NET-qualified candidates get a funded JRF slot in the first place.

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Add a contingency grant of roughly Rs 10,000 a year for humanities and social science scholars, plus HRA where applicable. If you do not clear JRF, ICSSR doctoral fellowships pay less: Rs 20,000 a month plus Rs 20,000 a year contingency, for a two-year full term.
figures.text: Add a contingency grant of roughly Rs 10,000 a year for humanities and social science scholars, plus HRA where applicable. If you do not clear JRF, ICSSR doctoral fellowships pay less: Rs 20,000 a month plus Rs 20,000 a year contingency, for a two-year full term.

figures.label: Allowance Amount Reported
figures.source: Government college assistant professor basic pay starts near Rs 57,700 (Level 10), roughly Rs 90,000-1.1 lakh gross with allowances once you get a post. Private college pay is commonly Rs 40,000-60,000 a month for the same role, and the number of PhD graduates each year in India comfortably exceeds the number of new permanent posts.
